title: Brother and sister creatures

segments.voice: Yesterday, perfect joy: shut out in the snow, and patient. Your line was perfect joy. Did a door close on you, and did you skip the speech? Day one thousand one hundred thirty.

Laudato si', mi' Signore. Praised be you, my Lord. That's the refrain of a song Francis made in the everyday Italian of his own region. Tradition says he made it late in life, when he was ill and could hardly see. It's called the Canticle of the Creatures, or the Canticle of Brother Sun, and it does something unusual. It doesn't just list the sun among God's works. It calls him Brother Sun. Then Sister Moon and the stars. Brother Wind. Sister Water. Brother Fire. Sister, and Mother, Earth. Every creature he names, he names as family. Today: brother and sister creatures.

Listen to how he describes them. Sister Water is useful and humble and precious and pure. Brother Fire is beautiful and cheerful, strong, and lights up the night. Sister Mother Earth feeds us, and brings out fruit and colored flowers and grass. Each one gets a small portrait, as if Francis knew them personally. And the little word in each line, per, can be heard more than one way: praised be you for Brother Sun, or by him, or through him. Readers take it differently, and the song may hold all three. Where does this come from? The Bible already has creation singing. Psalm one hundred forty-eight calls on everything to praise: "Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light." Francis takes one step further and gives them family names. The Little Flowers has stories to match. Francis preaches to a crowd of birds, telling them to thank God for their feathers and the air, and they stay to listen. Near the town of Gubbio a wolf has been terrifying the people. Francis goes out to meet him, calls him Brother Wolf, and makes peace: the wolf stops attacking, and the town agrees to feed him. Then, tradition says, near the very end Francis added one more verse, for one more relative: Sister Bodily Death, whom no one living can escape. Even she is family. That's the reach of the idea. If the sun, the wolf and even death are your siblings, nothing in the world is just a thing.

Here's the practice: thank a creature. Sit, and bring to mind one creature you've met today or will: a dog, a tree outside the window, the water in your glass, the sun on the floor. Give it Francis's kind of name for a moment. Brother Tree. Sister Water. Notice what it does for you without being asked. Then thank it, silently or out loud. If you pray, you can praise God through it, the way the Canticle does. The bell holds the time.
Brother and sister creatures. Francis's way of seeing sun, water, wolf and even death as family, in one household of praise.
Your line: family of creation. Today, say thank you out loud to one creature: the plant you water, the bird outside, the water from the tap. Day one thousand one hundred thirty.

howItsDone: Christians sing or pray Francis's Canticle of the Creatures, sometimes in hymn versions, and some churches bless animals on or near his feast day.
